resolved_suspects.description: Watcom loop-unrolled memcpy (countdown for-loop with the `(uint)bool * -N + M` direction idiom — Watcom's REP MOVSD lowering fingerprint). Replace the whole loop with memcpy(dst, src, count * stride) or a struct assignment in a .keep.

Watcom loop-unrolled memcpy (countdown for-loop with the `(uint)bool * -N + M` direction idiom — Watcom's REP MOVSD lowering fingerprint). Replace the whole loop with memcpy(dst, src, count * stride) or a struct assignment in a .keep.

Watcom loop-unrolled memcpy (countdown for-loop with the `(uint)bool * -N + M` direction idiom — Watcom's REP MOVSD lowering fingerprint). Replace the whole loop with memcpy(dst, src, count * stride) or a struct assignment in a .keep.

Watcom loop-unrolled memcpy (constant-count countdown loop with a cast-dword store `*(uint *)dst = *(uint *)src;` and both pointers stepped by +4 — REP MOVSD lowering with a baked-in dword count). Replace the loop with memcpy(dst, src, count * 4) in a .keep.
Watcom field-by-field struct copy (3 consecutive `dst.field = src.field;` lines). Replace with `dst = src;` or `memcpy(&dst, &src, sizeof(...));` in a .keep.

Watcom shadow-pointer walk — `pCVar10` self-updates via array-decay of a sibling array field whose byte offset equals the element stride. Replace `pCVar10->some_field[0]` reads with direct indexing on the original pointer; drop the shadow init and self-update.

Watcom shadow-pointer walk — `pCVar4` self-updates via array-decay of a sibling array field whose byte offset equals the element stride. Replace `pCVar4->some_field[0]` reads with direct indexing on the original pointer; drop the shadow init and self-update.

Watcom shadow-pointer walk — `pCVar3` self-updates via the address of a constant index into itself plus a subfield path, where `N*sizeof(*pCVar3) + offsetof(subfield)` equals the real array stride. Replace `pCVar3->some_field[0]` (or the zero-index access) reads with direct indexing on the original pointer; drop the shadow init and self-update.

Watcom shadow-pointer walk — `pCVar2` self-updates via the address of a constant index into itself plus a subfield path, where `N*sizeof(*pCVar2) + offsetof(subfield)` equals the real array stride. Replace `pCVar2->some_field[0]` (or the zero-index access) reads with direct indexing on the original pointer; drop the shadow init and self-update.
